key_insight: Nonlinear surface acoustic waves can generate, restructure, and nonthermally anneal near-surface dislocations in platinum while creating permanent atomic-scale roughness.
engineering_relevance: Acoustic processing could enable control of platinum’s near-surface microstructure and surface morphology, with potential relevance to catalysis.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of nonlinear Rayleigh waves in platinum.
Comparison of wave sharpening and dissipation on Pt(111) and Pt(001).
Tracking dislocation nucleation, reactions, and surface changes across repeated wave passages.
evidence_signal: Simulations show rapid shock formation on Pt(111), Shockley partial emission near the theoretical shear strength, and progressive dislocation-density reduction under repeated wave passages.
watch_item: The findings are simulation-based and strongly orientation-dependent; experimental processing conditions and catalytic benefits remain to be established.
paper_title: Generation and non-thermal annealing of dislocations and atomic-scale roughness by nonlinear surface acoustic waves
